newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico reduces number of airports for sale - gov't.
newsitem.headline: Mexico reduces number of airports for sale - gov't.

text.p: The Mexican government has decided to reduce the number of airports up for privatization, at least in the short-term, to 38 from 58 airports scheduled for sale within the next two years, officials from the Communication and Transport Ministry said Wednesday.

The government has not halted its plans to privatize the nation's airports, they said, although a committee overseeing privatizations chose to remove 20 of the country's smaller, more regional airports from the auction block. The regional sites are expected to be more difficult to sell to private companies.

Airport privatization details are expected in the first three months of the year, ministry spokesmen have said. The government has said private companies could more profitably manage and improve the nation's airports.
Mexico's four largest airports, in Mexico City, Cancun, Guadalajara and Monterrey, are still scheduled for privatization.
